method.input: Shared visible-playtest driver, normal menu clicks, movement, look, fire, aim, reload, sprint, dash and hold-E controls.
method.pause_disclosure: Live screenshots were captured and then ordinary Escape paused the game after almost every short action. I inspected screenshots and chose the next action while paused. This substantially aids aiming decisions, route interpretation and reaction time compared with continuous play.
method.allowed_observations: Visible screenshots, visible UI text returned by the driver, and helper --help only. No game source, tests, prior reviews, hidden game state, custom browser scripts or alternate URLs were read or used.
method.graphics: Driver reported Software-WebGL fallback enabled; renderer not certified.

Two attempts by one reviewer, with learning carried from the first into the second.
This is a provisional whole-game opinion from actual play, not a difficulty balance benchmark or a score-target exercise.
I completed the mission but did not explore every possible route or fight every enemy.

ratings_out_of_10.scope: Same provisional whole-game scope for every rating: briefing, combat and acquisition, all three memories, return, extraction, success/failure screens and restored records as personally observed.
ratings_out_of_10.rationale: A complete, coherent short mission with understandable goals, satisfying optic kills and a useful interrupt dash. The second attempt rewarded learning, but also let me recover two later memories and cross most of the arena while leaving many threats alive. Presentation has a strong restrained cyan/amber identity, rain, wet ground and consistent menus; repeated simple building and enemy forms, sparse environmental detail, tiny combat cues and the very compact mission keep it far from an AAA-ready whole game. These ratings do not certify audio, continuous mouse feel or rendering performance.

findings.observation: The opening warden is centered, its optic is obvious, and the opening instruction gives several valid tactics. Aimed optic shots produced clear CRITICAL elimination feedback. The successful Phase Break also explicitly confirmed a canceled shot.

Several small amber edge boxes, symbols and counts competed for attention around the west receiver and during the return. I relied more on actual orange optics than those cues. Partly screened small enemies were difficult to acquire, and I used many paused aim adjustments with low resulting accuracy. This reflects both the visual challenge and the driver's noncontinuous control method.

MOVE CLOSER / STEP INSIDE THE FLOOR RING gave actionable feedback before recovery. The cyan marker, waist-high named receiver, numbered memory slots, named memory card and supply-restore message made each successful acquisition clear. Brief personal records gave the objective a human reason, and could be reread after completion.

Objective labels remained clear even through walls, but that bearing did not identify the walkable route. I collided with a west wall and later the induction block on return. The briefing does explain side aisles, and moving sideways revealed one quickly, so this was recoverable rather than a blocker.

My first exposed recovery led to a fast death, but clearing the two west sentinels changed the second attempt substantially. I then recovered east and Heart, ran back and held extraction with only one further elimination. The full successful run took 51 in-game seconds. That offered a clear learning payoff but limited the sustained combat depth demonstrated by this playthrough.

Typography, teal panels, amber hazards and wet rainy courtyard form a consistent identity. Failure and victory both provide clear closure and readable statistics. The restored-records dialog fits all three memories visibly without truncation at the observed screenshot size.
